Description: NATO UNCLASSIFIED RFP-ACT-SACT-26-02C LABOR CATEGORY 52: SPACE PROGRAMME SENIOR MANAGEMENT SUPPORT Location: Norfolk VA, USA (On-site) Number of Candidates: One (1) candidate required Period of Performance: Base Period: Award – 31 December 2026 with four potential 12 – month options Option Year 1: 1 January 2027 – 31 December 2027 Option Year 2: 1 January 2028 – 31 December 2028 Option Year 3: 1 January 2029 – 31 December 2029 Option Year 4: 1 January 2030 – 31 December 2030 Tasking 1. Support the ACT Space Branch PMT in the delivery, synchronization, and implementation of the NATO Space Capability Programme (CPP) across all tranches and associated projects. 2. Coordinate programme execution activities between HQ SACT, SHAPE, AIRCOM Space Theatre Component (STC), NCIA, NSPA, nations and commercial partners. 3. Support the development, refinement, and implementation of programme artefacts, including project proposals, implementation plans, programme reviews, risk registers, dashboards, and capability roadmaps. 4. Contribute to programme governance activities, PMT meetings, Bi-SC coordination mechanisms, and senior leader engagements. 6. Support the identification, analysis and mitigation of programme risks, interdependencies, and critical paths across all space projects. 7. Support experimentation, wargaming, operational demonstrations and exercises, including Arctic Sentry, Cosmic Sentinel, and/or related activities. 8. Coordinate with NCIA architects PMT SMEs, and national experts to maintain programme coherence and support architecture development and analysis of alternatives. 9. Support engagement with industry and commercial space actors in support of NATO Commercial Space Strategy implementation. NATO UNCLASSIFIED RFP-ACT-SACT-26-02C 10. Produce reports, briefings, and recommendations for ACT Space Branch leadership. 11. Directly supports the Branch Head CR and will be required to travel to meetings and conferences both within and outside NATO’s boundaries for up to 30 days per year. 12. Performs additional tasks as required by the COTR related to the LABOR category. Essential Qualifications 1. A University/ Bachelor’s degree in Science. 2. Minimum 5 years’ experience within NATO capability development, programme management, or defence acquisition. 3. Demonstrated knowledge of NATO Space policy, CPP governance and PMT processes. 4. Demonstrate a minimum of 3 years operational knowledge of C2 systems within the last 10 years either as a military officer or as a civilian. 5. Demonstrate a minimum of 3 years in the last 10 years a sound knowledge of Capability Development and Management processes in the C2 area. 6. Experience supporting multinational programmes and senior-level governance bodies. 7. Programme and Project Management experience in the past 10 years within a complex and dynamic programme environment. 8. Working knowledge of Configuration Management methods and practices. 9.
